title: Prompt bloat after a retrieval change
source: Live calls to Token Factory (Nemotron-3.5 Lightning)

events.detail: retrieval top_k raised from 2 to 600 chunks

evidence.claim: Input tokens increased 261x from baseline (~213) to incident (~55,721), while concurrency and retries remained unchanged
Deploy event shows retrieval top_k raised from 2 to 600 chunks, directly causing prompt expansion
Latency scales with input token bucket: 0-500 tokens = 0.39s (baseline) vs 4000+ tokens = 0.73s (incident)
Holding retries fixed (0-1), latency rises with input_tokens: 0.39s → 0.73s
Holding concurrency fixed (0-2), latency rises with input_tokens: 0.39s → 0.73s
No retry storm: 100% of requests have 0 retries in both windows
No concurrency change between windows: avg_concurrency=1 in both; only one concurrency bucket (0-2) observed in each window
Latency by concurrency shows same single bucket 0-2 in both windows with latency matching input-token buckets
Stratified test varying input_tokens while holding concurrency fixed confirms input_tokens drives latency

rejected_hypotheses.why_rejected: No concurrency variation exists in either window (avg=1, only bucket 0-2); latency difference correlates with input_tokens not concurrency. Cannot test within-window concurrency effect due to no concurrency variation, but cross-window comparison shows latency moves with input_tokens while concurrency is constant.
0 retries in 100% of requests in both windows; retry_breakdown shows no retries at all
Latency increase correlates perfectly with input token increase; TTFT equals total latency in both windows, indicating processing time scales with input size, not provider degradation

uncertainties: Exact token-per-chunk ratio not quantified, but top_k 2→600 implies ~300x context expansion matching observed 261x token increase
Cannot test within-window concurrency effect because concurrency does not vary in the data; however, cross-window evidence strongly favors input_tokens as the driver
recommended_actions: Roll back retrieval top_k from 600 to 2 (or a lower value) to reduce input token volume
Implement input token budget/cap to prevent future prompt expansion incidents
Add monitoring alert on avg_input_tokens threshold
